correctness.rationale: Fink exact recursive-divisor identity reduces pristine to P_d(c)=q^d. For odd d the squared-binomial alternating sum at X=-d-1 vanishes, implying Q_d integer polynomial. Writing m=c+d+1 gives m Q_d(c)=d! q^d; as P_d(c)>m, Q_d(c)>d!. When q does not divide K_d, q dividing m would force Q_d(c) coprime to q and hence Q_d(c)|d!, contradiction. Thus either m|d! or q|K_d. An independently implemented exact-arithmetic exhaustive verification enumerated all 639114 relevant m|d! candidate c values and precisely the complete odd prime factors of each K_d (K factorization has no residual prime), testing exact integer dth powers and monotone exception equations; no cases survive for all nine exponents. Independently computed K via critical-point derivative sum. This is exhaustive only by the unrestricted two-branch proof, not a finite scan of arbitrary c bound.
